bug_semantics: OAuthHelpers.parseAuthRequest extracted redirect_uri from the authorize query and returned it without checking that it was in the registered client's redirectUris. completeAuthorization then built the 302 Location from that attacker-controlled URI and attached the authorization code. The token endpoint did check redirect_uri against the allowlist, but that is too late: if an application auto-approved a previously authorized client_id, a victim could be sent to a malicious callback with a live code. CWE-601; GHSA-4pc9-x2fx-p7vj / CVE-2025-4143 (PUBLISHED, not withdrawn); affected @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider < 0.0.5, patched in 0.0.5 via PR #26.
flaw_origin: Root commit 3b2ae809e9256d292079bb15ea9fe49439a0779c first wrote oauth-provider.ts. parseAuthRequest (lines 661-676) copied redirect_uri from the query and returned it with no client lookup or allowlist check; completeAuthorization (line 711) redirected to options.request.redirectUri; only handleAuthorizationCodeGrant (lines 292-301) compared redirect_uri to clientInfo.redirectUris. That is the exact incomplete OAuth check later described in the advisory. 11fcf4f9b18ace3ecf5da6581c0685d4bb401028 later moved the same parser body from a closure to OAuthHelpersImpl (refactor, not a first-write). No public parent exists to hold a prior version of these lines.

reasoning: CVE-2025-4143 is a real, still-published CWE-601: workers-oauth-provider did not validate authorize-endpoint redirect_uri against the client's registered URIs, while it did validate at token exchange. The attack needs an application that auto-approves a previously authorized client, then redirects the victim to the unvalidated callback with a code. The first public write of that incomplete authorize path is root commit 3b2ae809e9256d292079bb15ea9fe49439a0779c (oauth-provider.ts parseAuthRequest + completeAuthorization using the parsed URI, with the token-side allowlist already present). git rev-list --parents shows no parent, so the lines cannot pre-exist; 11fcf4f is a class-conversion refactor of the same parser and 941684c is a path move, so neither is the BIC. No finer public member of the root commit is reconstructable. The check lands in 66de8d802c1d7c468887906ea1a0769a975ff1e3 and on main via merge 4393dd4f96159f261629ce80e9ecaa027d348131 (PR #26), then in npm 0.0.5 (317fdfd / PR #28), after v0.0.4 which still lacks the check. AI role is judged only from the BIC commit object: the subject and body state that Claude wrote the library from the included prompt; author/committer is human Kenton Varda with no trailers. That is commit-object AI authorship of the first write of the flawed mechanism, so the verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
